facts.value: Scene entry requests fog animation frame 0, evaluates it, and registers this callback at process priority 0x17. Subsequent invocations delegate to the fog's AObj interpreter. A null AObj or AOBJ_NO_ANIM returns immediately; first play evaluates without advancing, otherwise curr_frame advances by framerate. Looping playback wraps when rewind_frame is below end_frame and otherwise clamps to end_frame. AOBJ_NO_UPDATE passes a null update callback to ordinary FObj interpretation, but loop-boundary and terminal HSD_FObjStopAnimAll calls still receive the original update callback. Completed non-looping playback sets AOBJ_NO_ANIM.
facts.rationale: Preserves the useful playback explanation while restricting NO_UPDATE suppression to the call actually guarded by that flag, rather than asserting unconditional suppression of all property updates.

evidence.why: Playback branches and exact scope of callback suppression.

facts.value: The sequence has separate model and camera animation timelines. After updating the lead model, exact frame 251 independently destroys and clears each non-null temporary Koopa/stand GObj and then invokes the Giga Bowser reveal initializer regardless of those pointer values; there is no local once-only latch. The initializer creates model 1 at frame 251, configures CKIND_GKOOPS in player slot 1 and initializes audio. Independently, after camera animation updates, exact frames 130 and 190 request rumble effect 0xD with duration argument 0, and exact frame 251 requests effect 1 with duration argument 0xDB. A separate exact end-frame guard performs rumble cleanup and requests scene exit, so a cue and completion can execute on the same tick. The scene-frame callback separately delegates Start-triggered skipping to the common visual-scene handler.
facts.rationale: Corrects the misleading description of the camera cue as the transformation event and preserves independent guards, update-before-test ordering, repeat-trigger possibility and the separate input path.

evidence.why: Reveal initializer and independent guarded temporary-object teardown.
Camera cues and independent completion guard.
Rumble effect/duration semantics and all-controller cleanup.
